newsitem.title: USA: Louisiana oil pipeline may reopen Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Louisiana oil pipeline may reopen Wednesday.

text.p: A damaged Texaco pipeline, shut down since it ruptured on Friday, may reopen on Wednesday as work continues to clean 5,000 barrels of crude oil from a fragile coastal marsh, a company spokesman said.
Repairs were completed late on Tuesday on the damaged 40-foot section of the 42-mile pipeline and line testing began on Wednesday morning, Texaco spokesman Pierre DeGruy told Reuters.
"We anticipate being back on-line later today, if everything tests out," he said.

An estimated 2,500 barrels have been recovered to date, he said, adding that Tuesday figures citing that amount were later revised downward. Authorities estimate that between 30 percent and 50 percent of the oil is evaporating.
"We're continuing the intensive, but rather passive task of cleaning up the marsh without causing further damage by treading all over it," DeGruy said.
"High tide last night flushed a lot of oil out of the marsh where we can get to it better," DeGruy said.
The rupture occurred late Friday in Lake Barre in Terrebonne Parish, about 40 miles southwest of New Orleans.
Louisiana Department of Environmental Quality spokesman Kerry St. Pe said the delicate plants kept that area of the Louisiana marsh intact and they would die if submerged in oily water.
"One of our roles is to guide the cleanup so it isn't more damaging than the oil in a critically eroding area," he said.
DeGruy said the impact on wildlife appeared minimal. The Coast Guard reported only nine birds seen with oil on them.

State health officials on Tuesday closed a number of oyster beds as a precautionary measure and shrimpers and other fishermen also were kept out of the cleanup area. The state will test seafood on Wednesday to determine if any has been contaminated.
